item.title: 'Now is the time of monsters': How religious leaders are failing their moral duty
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description: From rabbis sanctioning a holy war to a Pope who won't name the aggressor, the world's great religions are facing a crisis of conscience over Gaza. Is their silence and complicity creating a Judaism without a soul and a Christianity without a heart?

item.title: The day the UN walked out of New York: How the UN lost its will to defy the US
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: In 1988, the UN forced Washington to its knees by moving to Geneva so Yasser Arafat could speak. Today, as the US blocks Palestinian leaders and arms Israel’s genocide in Gaza, the Assembly stays silent. Has the UN lost its courage?

item.title: 'Faith, land and gold': The making of American culture
item.author: Alex Liberto
item.description: The relentless drive for faith, land and gold propelled a diverse people across a continent, creating an American culture from the collision of European traditions, African resilience and the raw wilderness itself.

item.title: The broken covenant: When belief betrays and the faithful must rebel
item.description: At its heart, faith is a promise—a covenant of justice, refuge and truth. But across the world, that covenant lies in pieces, shattered by leaders who offer platitudes for violence and dogma as a shield for indifference. From this betrayal, however, a rebellion of conscience is rising.

item.title: Caravaggio’s two Matthews: Realism rejected, revelation remade
item.author: Carla Pietrobattista
item.description: Between 1600 and 1601, Caravaggio recast the scene: out went the coarse, patron-spurned Matthew and dominating angel; in came classical dress, a lighter touch and a writer in charge.

item.title: The hidden war on honeybees: Murder hornets, parasitic wasps and the fight for survival
item.author: Partho Pratim Chatterjee
item.description: From hornets that can wipe out entire hives in under two hours to wasps that hollow bees from within, invasive predators are undermining apiculture worldwide.

item.title: Open letter to the UN: Protect press freedom and defend human rights
item.author: UN-aligned
item.description: The deliberate persecution of journalists is spreading unchecked across the world. Without urgent and enforceable action, the UN risks abandoning its founding values of dignity, justice and truth.

item.title: The prophets of annihilation’: Inside the movement that sees genocide as god's will
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: For millions of Christian Zionists, the annihilation of Palestinians is not a crime to be condemned, but a sacred prophecy to be fulfilled. This is the story of the theological engine driving the war on Gaza.

item.title: 89 seconds to midnight: The cost of lost empathy
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description: Our greatest threat lies not only in nuclear arms or climate collapse but in the death of empathy itself. Unless we confront the four horsemen of exploitation, greed, colonialism and nationalism, nature will deliver the reckoning we refuse to face.

item.title: World federalism is the key to ending functional illiteracy and reviving civilisation
item.author: Omar Alansari-Kreger
item.description: In an age of abundant technology yet persistent functional illiteracy, world federalism asks what it truly means to be civilized and how global literacy can enable a continuous human renaissance.

item.title: "I entrust you with Palestine": A murdered Gaza journalist pleads amid his people’s erasure
item.author: Anas Al-Sharif
item.description: Israel succeeded in killing journalist Anas Jamal Al-Sharif, but it could not silence him. In this posthumous letter, he testifies against those who "accepted our killing," and entrusts his beloved daughter Sham, his son Salah, and the soul of his nation to a world he urges to finally act.

item.title: The Zionist experiment has failed: it must be abolished
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: Far from an aberration, Israel’s genocide is the fulfilment of its design. The era of two-state fantasies is over. Only a single, secular republic offers justice.

item.title: When Kakistocracy Sanctions Humanity
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description: US sanctions UN investigator Francesca Albanese for speaking out on Gaza, punishing her for naming those profiting from violence while the world watches in quiet complicity.

item.title: Another US veto condemns Gaza to further genocide
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description: As Trump and Netanyahu cosy up in Washington again with fresh talks on Gaza, one thing is certain: there is no Israeli atrocity, however diabolical, that the US will not back. Here I pick at Dorothy Shea’s narrative after yet another US veto blocking moves to put an end to the genocide.

item.title: Nicaragua’s War on the Press: New Report Highlights Escalating Repression
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description:
UN-aligned recently partnered with FLED Nicaragua to translate their annual report from Spanish into English, highlighting the grave state of press freedom in the country.

The assassination of retired Nicaraguan army officer and outspoken critic of President Daniel Ortega, Roberto Samcam, on June 19 while in exile in Costa Rica, underscores the urgency of the crisis and the critical need to raise international awareness.

Read full report ->

item.title: Sky-Born Infernos: How Pyrocumulonimbus Clouds Supercharge Wildfires
item.author: Partho Pratim Chatterjee
item.description: Born from wildfire heat, pyrocumulonimbus clouds unleash lightning, fierce winds, and towering smoke plumes. As the climate warms, these explosive storm systems are becoming ever more frequent and deadly.

item.title: Confronting a Genocide
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description: Despite the “business as usual” attitude of most of the world’s politicians and the people the media like to keep in the spotlight, the genocidaires are hurting. The protests, the immolations, the hunger strikes, the courageous acts of defiance… They are slowly taking their toll.

item.title: More than Just a Gay Icon: Edmund White (1940-2025)
item.author: Alex Liberto
item.description: June began with the death of two literary giants: Edmund White (died June 3, 2025 at 85) and Frederick Forsyth (died June 9,2025 at 86). Our literary editor, Alex Liberto, had met and corresponded with the former and has written this touching tribute.

item.title: ‘Held Hostage No More’: Harris, Democrats and the Price of Betrayal
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: Harris’s defeat is no tragedy; it’s a sliver of justice, a rare rebuke from voters who refuse to reward American indifference to suffering abroad.

item.title: ‘Reaping what you sow’: Why Trump’s assassination attempt is unworthy to steal headlines
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: The shooting in Pennsylvania is the fruit of the toxic tree Trump, and consecutive US administrations, have cultivated. It's time our headlines focus on what actually matters.

item.title: ‘If it ain’t broke... break it’: How the US betrayed free speech and the First Amendment
item.author: Adrian Liberto
item.description: From hounding WikiLeaks' Assange to stifling peaceful students protesting genocide, America has abandoned its democratic values along with all notions of decency.

item.title: “We’ve seen this before”: Inside Israel’s war on truth, journalists and the free media
item.author: Ariana Yekrangi
item.description: Amidst rising violence and a tightening grip on truth, Israel's aggressive campaign against journalists mirrors tactics used by history's most oppressive regimes.
